title: Symphonie fantastique
hook: An obsession told in five scenes, ending at a witches’ sabbath.

painting.title: Witches’ Sabbath, or the Great He-Goat
painting.pairingNote: Painted within a decade of the symphony, the same nightmare gathering that Berlioz stages in his finale.
painting.medium: Oil on mural, transferred to canvas

facts: First performed on 5 December 1830 in Paris. Berlioz was 26. Beethoven had died only three years earlier.
It is [[programme-music|programme music]]: Berlioz handed the audience a written story. A young artist, hopelessly in love, takes opium and dreams.
The beloved is represented by one melody, the [[idee-fixe|idée fixe]], which returns in every movement in a new disguise.
The inspiration was Berlioz’s own obsession with the actress Harriet Smithson, whom he later married.
The orchestra was enormous and new: two harps, bells, four timpani, an English horn, a shrill small clarinet.
bigPicture.inOneLine: longing (I), a ball (II), the countryside (III), the scaffold (IV), the sabbath (V).

movements.heading: Rêveries – Passions
movements.title: Rêveries – Passions
movements.tempo: Largo – Allegro agitato e appassionato assai
movements.summary: The artist drifts in vague longing, then sees the beloved. From that moment her melody will not leave him.

mainIdeas.description: The [[idee-fixe|idée fixe]]: a long, yearning melody for flute and violins that rises in waves and falls back.

stops.hear: Soft woodwinds, then [[muted|muted]] violins in a slow, sad melody with long pauses
stops.happening: The introduction: daydreams and melancholy

stops.hear: Flute and violins together in a long, restless melody over a nervous, heartbeat-like accompaniment
stops.happening: The idée fixe. The beloved appears

stops.label: Middle
stops.hear: The melody is broken into pieces; strings slide up and down in waves; sudden silences
stops.happening: Jealousy and agitation

stops.hear: The idée fixe blazes out in the full orchestra
stops.happening: The peak of passion

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Slow, soft, organ-like chords
stops.happening: Berlioz marks this “religiously”. The artist seeks consolation

movements.heading: Un bal
movements.title: Un bal (A Ball)
movements.summary: A glittering waltz at a ball. In the middle of the crowd, he sees her again.

stops.hear: Shimmering strings and rippling harps, growing brighter
stops.happening: The ballroom comes into focus

stops.hear: Violins sweep into an elegant waltz
stops.happening: The dance

stops.hear: Flute and oboe play the idée fixe, now in waltz time, while the dance murmurs on below
stops.happening: She appears among the dancers

stops.hear: The waltz returns, fuller and faster
stops.happening: The whirl resumes

stops.label: Near the end
stops.hear: A solo clarinet recalls the idée fixe; then a headlong finish
stops.happening: One last glimpse before the dance sweeps her away

movements.heading: Scène aux champs
movements.title: Scène aux champs (Scene in the Fields)
movements.summary: An evening in the country. Two shepherds call to each other; the artist finds calm, then doubt returns. The longest and stillest movement.

stops.hear: An English horn calls; an oboe answers from far away (offstage)
stops.happening: Two shepherds piping across a valley

stops.hear: A broad, calm melody for flute and violins
stops.happening: The peace of the countryside

stops.hear: The idée fixe in the woodwinds against angry, muttering low strings, rising to an outburst
stops.happening: “What if she is deceiving me?” The storm is inside him

stops.hear: The calm melody returns, decorated
stops.happening: Peace, but shaken

stops.label: Last 2 minutes
stops.hear: The English horn calls again. No answer. Only soft rolls from four timpani
stops.happening: Distant thunder, solitude, silence. One of the most original pages of orchestration of its time

movements.heading: Marche au supplice
movements.title: Marche au supplice (March to the Scaffold)
movements.summary: The dream turns to nightmare. He has killed his beloved, is condemned, and is marched to the guillotine.

stops.hear: Muffled drums and growling horns
stops.happening: The procession approaches

stops.hear: Cellos and basses stride down a long scale, grim and heavy
stops.happening: Theme 1: the march of the condemned. A bassoon soon adds a mocking counter-melody

stops.hear: Blazing brass and winds in a swaggering tune
stops.happening: Theme 2: the crowd’s march, brilliant and brutal

stops.label: Last 30 seconds
stops.hear: A solo clarinet begins the idée fixe, tenderly
stops.happening: “A last thought of love”

stops.label: Immediately after
stops.hear: A crashing chord; plucked strings; drum rolls and brass
stops.happening: The blade falls, the head drops, the crowd roars

notice: The clarinet gets only the first few notes of the idée fixe before it is cut off. That is the story in four seconds.

movements.heading: Songe d'une nuit du sabbat
movements.title: Songe d'une nuit du sabbat (Dream of a Witches' Sabbath)
movements.summary: He sees himself at a witches’ sabbath, gathered for his own funeral. The beloved arrives, now a grotesque parody. The most radical music in the symphony.

stops.hear: Eerie high strings, low growls, cackling slides in the woodwinds
stops.happening: The gathering of witches and spirits

stops.hear: A squealing small clarinet plays a jerky, trilling jig
stops.happening: The idée fixe, turned vulgar. The beloved has become a witch; the orchestra roars its welcome

stops.hear: Deep bells toll
stops.happening: The funeral bells

stops.hear: Tubas and bassoons intone a slow, ancient chant; brass repeat it faster; woodwinds mock it
stops.happening: The [[dies-irae|Dies irae]], the medieval chant for the dead, parodied

stops.hear: A stamping dance tune starts in the low strings and spreads upward
stops.happening: The witches’ round dance, written as a [[fugue|fugue]]

stops.hear: The dance in the strings and the Dies irae in the brass, at the same time
stops.happening: The two themes combined

stops.hear: A dry, clattering sound from the violins
stops.happening: [[col-legno|Col legno]]: the players tap the strings with the wood of the bow, like rattling bones

stops.label: Last minute
stops.hear: Brass and drums in a blazing finish
stops.happening: The orgy ends in a C major that sounds anything but innocent

threads.title: One melody, five masks
threads.body: Follow the idée fixe: noble (I), dancing (II), anxious (III), cut off (IV), grotesque (V).

threads.title: Sound as story
threads.body: Offstage oboe, four timpani as thunder, bells, col legno: each effect has a meaning in the tale.

threads.title: A new kind of symphony
threads.body: A symphony that tells an explicit story was a turning point for the whole century.
